preferred_translation: they discern: there is no more of this state of being
alternative_translations: they clearly know: there is no more of this state of being
they understand: there is no more of this state of being
definition: Arahant-declaration formula surface using pajānāti on the release side; governed here so the verb does not drift into vague realization rhetoric.
notes: This formula inherits the pajānāti policy while sitting in liberation-side prose. SN 22.86 supports the formula surface directly, in the exact form quoted here; DN 2 has the same declaration with the quotation particle written separately. MN 36, which this record cited until 2026-09-11, gives the same declaration in the Buddha's first-person awakening account with abbhaññāsiṁ, from abhijānāti, rather than pajānāti; that line follows the abhijānāti policy and is not an instance of this record. Keep the line plain and decisive. Do not inflate it into imported enlightenment-talk or soften it into bland understanding if the sharper verbal force can still be heard.

example_phrases.translation: they discern: there is no more of this state of being
example_phrases.notes: Recurring formula in arahant declarations. The SN 22.86 surface renders the full line `They discern: 'Birth is worn away, the spiritual life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.'`

authority_basis.scope: Supports the release-side pajānāti formula in arahant declarations.

translation_policy.default_scope: Use 'they discern: there is no more of this state of being' as the default rendering when this formula is translated directly.
translation_policy.when_not_to_apply: Use the controlled alternates only when the immediate English context requires it. Do not inflate the formula into generic realization or enlightenment rhetoric. Where the source uses abhijānāti instead of pajānāti, as in MN 36, follow the abhijānāti record.
translation_policy.drift_risk: Prevents pajānāti in liberation formulas from drifting into vague realization-language or imported attainment slogans.
